p: These four programs share one shape: parse at the edge, compute with a single pass or a driven table, and return a shape that makes the empty and invalid cases impossible to ignore. That shape is what makes the rest of this part readable — every program from here on follows it.

The pattern across this chapter is that a Map plus one loop beats a chain of array methods whenever you need grouping, deduplication or counting. Array chains are clearer for filtering and mapping; Maps are the right accumulator for anything that folds many items into fewer buckets.

s.t: Wrappers that change when or how often a function runs

chapters.c: Programs: Objects, Classes and Data Structures

p: The through-line for all asynchronous code is that every await needs a bound: a timeout, an attempt limit, a concurrency limit or a signal. Unbounded waiting is the failure mode that turns a slow dependency into an outage, and adding the bound is usually four lines.

The browser programs in this chapter all follow the same discipline: build nodes rather than concatenating HTML, set `textContent` for anything a user typed, keep state in one object with a single render, and cancel in-flight asynchronous work when the input changes.

Every one of these programs is built from the same ingredients: a bounded read, an explicit error type, a single place where the boundary is crossed, and cancellation. That is what makes a tool safe to run on data you did not create.
